cards.statement: A Deployment's RollingUpdate strategy can bound extra and unavailable Pods during replacement.
cards.explanation: RollingUpdate uses separate bounds for extra Pods and unavailable Pods, letting a Deployment replace replicas gradually.

cards.statement: A Deployment's Recreate strategy starts replacement Pods before removing the old Pods.
cards.explanation: During a Recreate upgrade, the Deployment terminates the old revision's Pods before creating Pods for the new revision.
cards.misconception: Recreate overlaps old and replacement Pods during an upgrade.

cards.statement: A Deployment rollback restores the earlier Pod template from the current manifest file.
cards.explanation: A Deployment rollback selects an earlier recorded revision of its Pod template. The current manifest file is not the source of that revision.
cards.misconception: Rollback reconstructs a previous Deployment from the current manifest file.

cards.statement: In an Argo Rollouts blue-green rollout, the active Service routes traffic to the preview version during testing.
cards.explanation: Before promotion, the preview Service points to the new revision while the active Service continues pointing to the old revision.
cards.misconception: The active Service serves the preview revision before promotion.

cards.statement: A canary rollout sends a small share of live traffic to a new version beside the stable version.
cards.explanation: A canary introduces the new version to part of the live traffic while the stable version continues serving the rest.

cards.statement: A Helm chart packages templates and metadata for a related set of Kubernetes resources.
cards.explanation: A Helm chart groups the files needed to describe an application, including resource templates and chart metadata.

cards.statement: A Kustomize overlay can edit base resource files in place to create an environment variant.
cards.explanation: A Kustomize overlay applies changes on top of a reusable base. It does not need to modify the base files, which can serve other overlays.
cards.misconception: Kustomize produces variants by changing the base files themselves.

source.title: Declarative Management of Kubernetes Objects Using Kustomize

cards.statement: In OpenGitOps, software agents pull desired state from its source for deployment.
cards.explanation: The OpenGitOps Pulled Automatically principle assigns software agents the task of fetching desired-state declarations from their source.

cards.statement: In OpenGitOps, a saved desired-state revision may be edited after deployment.
cards.explanation: OpenGitOps calls for desired state to be stored with immutable revisions, versioning, and a complete history.
cards.misconception: GitOps permits changes to an already recorded desired-state revision.

cards.statement: Argo CD and Flux reconcile Kubernetes resources against a declared source of truth.
cards.explanation: Argo CD and Flux implement GitOps workflows that compare live Kubernetes resources with declared state and correct drift.

source.title: Argo and Flux: grown-up GitOps for cloud native generation

cards.statement: kubectl logs can target one container in a Pod that runs several containers.
cards.explanation: kubectl logs accepts a container selection when a Pod contains multiple containers, so its output can focus on one container.

cards.statement: kubectl logs shows a restarted container's previous instance by default.
cards.explanation: kubectl logs normally reads the current container instance. The previous instance's logs need an explicit selection.
cards.misconception: Previous container logs are the default after a restart.

cards.statement: kubectl describe includes Events associated with the resource being inspected.
cards.explanation: kubectl describe presents resource details together with related Events, which can reveal scheduling or runtime problems.

cards.statement: kubectl get events lists Event resources in the current Namespace by default.
cards.explanation: Events are namespaced resources. kubectl get events uses the current Namespace unless another Namespace or all Namespaces are requested.

cards.statement: kubectl exec starts a diagnostic command in a newly created Pod.
cards.explanation: kubectl exec runs a command inside a container of an existing Pod. It does not create a diagnostic Pod.
cards.misconception: kubectl exec creates a separate Pod for its command.

cards.statement: kubectl port-forward changes a Service to type NodePort while the tunnel is active.
cards.explanation: kubectl port-forward connects a local port to a Pod selected for the target. It does not change the Service's type.
cards.misconception: Port forwarding temporarily converts a Service into a NodePort Service.

cards.statement: kubectl debug can add an ephemeral diagnostic container to an existing Pod.
cards.explanation: An ephemeral container lets an operator bring debugging tools into a running Pod whose application image lacks them.

cards.statement: By default, kubectl rollout status watches the latest Deployment rollout until completion.
cards.explanation: kubectl rollout status waits for the latest rollout to finish and reports its progress as the Deployment changes.

cards.statement: kubectl rollout history lists previous container restarts for a Deployment.
cards.explanation: kubectl rollout history shows a Deployment's rollout revisions and their recorded configurations, not individual container restarts.
cards.misconception: Deployment rollout history is a record of container restarts.

cards.statement: Testing a Service DNS name on a laptop confirms that Pods can resolve the same name.
cards.explanation: A DNS lookup inside a Pod tests the cluster resolver and search settings used by workloads. A laptop lookup does not establish that Pod DNS works.
cards.misconception: Laptop DNS resolution proves that in-cluster Service DNS works for Pods.

cards.statement: In Prometheus's primary collection model, monitored targets push samples to the Prometheus server.
cards.explanation: Prometheus primarily collects metrics by scraping configured targets. Regular targets expose samples for Prometheus to fetch.
cards.misconception: Prometheus normally receives metrics pushed by monitored targets.

cards.statement: Each Prometheus time series is identified by a metric name and label set.
cards.explanation: Changing a label value creates a distinct Prometheus time series, even when the metric name stays the same.

cards.statement: PromQL can evaluate log entries alongside metric samples in a Prometheus query.
cards.explanation: PromQL queries Prometheus time series. It does not treat raw log entries as another input to a metrics expression.
cards.misconception: PromQL directly combines raw logs with metric samples.

cards.statement: Alertmanager groups and routes alerts emitted by Prometheus to configured receivers.
cards.explanation: Alertmanager handles alerts sent by Prometheus, grouping them and routing notifications to receivers such as email or paging systems.

cards.statement: OpenTelemetry APIs and SDKs provide code instrumentation for application telemetry.
cards.explanation: Applications use OpenTelemetry APIs and SDKs to create and emit telemetry through instrumentation.

cards.statement: The OpenTelemetry Collector stores traces as the system of record for later queries.
cards.explanation: The OpenTelemetry Collector receives, processes, and exports telemetry to backends. It is a pipeline component, not a queryable trace store.
cards.misconception: The Collector serves as the long-term trace database.

cards.statement: Kubernetes can write container stdout and stderr to a built-in cluster-wide log store.
cards.explanation: Kubernetes captures container output through node-level logging, but it provides no built-in cluster-wide log storage.
cards.misconception: Kubernetes includes central storage for container logs.

cards.statement: The Metrics API supplies CPU and memory usage to Kubernetes autoscalers.
cards.explanation: The Metrics API exposes basic Pod and Node resource usage for autoscaling. A metrics-server or another implementation serves the API.

cards.statement: Trace context propagation links spans across service boundaries in a distributed request.
cards.explanation: Passing trace context between services lets their spans be associated with the same distributed request.

cards.statement: An SLO is the raw measurement collected for a service's reliability target.
cards.explanation: An SLI measures service behavior. An SLO states the reliability objective associated with one or more SLIs.
cards.misconception: An SLO is the measurement rather than the objective.

cards.statement: CNCF's cloud native model confines application deployment to public cloud providers.
cards.explanation: CNCF describes cloud native technologies as usable in public, private, and hybrid clouds.
cards.misconception: Cloud native applications have to run in a public cloud.

cards.statement: A microservice's code update requires rebuilding and releasing every other service in the application.
cards.explanation: Microservices are separate deployable parts of an application. Teams can update and deploy one service independently of the others.
cards.misconception: Changing one microservice forces a rebuild and release of the entire application.

cards.statement: In immutable infrastructure, recreating a container from its image discards a manual filesystem hotfix.
cards.explanation: A change made inside one running container is absent from a new container created from the original image.

cards.statement: CNCF associates resilient cloud native systems with tightly coupled components.
cards.explanation: CNCF's cloud native description associates resilience with loosely coupled systems whose components have fewer dependencies.
cards.misconception: Tight coupling is a cloud native resilience principle.

cards.statement: When multiple metrics yield replica recommendations, a HorizontalPodAutoscaler chooses the largest.
cards.explanation: A HorizontalPodAutoscaler calculates desired replicas for each available metric and chooses the largest recommendation before applying its scaling rules.

cards.statement: A VerticalPodAutoscaler adjusts Pod resource requests based on usage patterns.
cards.explanation: A VerticalPodAutoscaler analyzes resource usage and recommends updated CPU or memory requests for targeted Pods.

cards.statement: Cluster Autoscaler creates a new Node group when pending Pods need capacity.
cards.explanation: Cluster Autoscaler adds Nodes to preconfigured Node groups when pending Pods need capacity; it does not create new Node groups.
cards.misconception: Cluster Autoscaler automatically provisions new Node groups.

cards.statement: Knative Serving can scale service Pods to zero after traffic stops.
cards.explanation: Knative Serving supports scaling idle services down to zero Pods and scaling them up when requests return.

cards.statement: A Kubernetes cluster can pair a CRI runtime, CNI network plugin, and CSI driver from separate vendors.
cards.explanation: CRI, CNI, and CSI define interfaces for runtimes, networking, and storage, allowing compatible implementations to be selected independently.

cards.statement: The CNCF Landscape treats an entry as a CNCF-hosted project once it appears on the map.
cards.explanation: The CNCF Landscape catalogs cloud native projects and products beyond CNCF-hosted projects. An entry does not grant project membership.
cards.misconception: Listing in the CNCF Landscape means CNCF hosts the project.

cards.statement: The CNCF operates as part of the Linux Foundation.
cards.explanation: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation is part of the nonprofit Linux Foundation, which hosts open source communities.

cards.statement: The CNCF Governing Board maintains technical roadmaps for hosted projects.
cards.explanation: The CNCF Governing Board handles marketing, business oversight, and budget decisions. Project technical direction belongs to the technical community.
cards.misconception: The Governing Board directs the technical roadmaps of CNCF projects.

cards.statement: The CNCF Technical Oversight Committee admits projects into CNCF.
cards.explanation: The Technical Oversight Committee evaluates and accepts projects into CNCF as part of its technical governance role.

cards.statement: TAG Observability is among CNCF's active Technical Advisory Groups.
cards.explanation: CNCF's current TAG roster places observability within TAG Operational Resilience; TAG Observability is a former group name.
cards.misconception: CNCF still has an active group named TAG Observability.
cards.volatilityNote: CNCF can reorganize or rename TAGs; checked against its current TAG roster on 2026-10-03.

cards.statement: The CNCF End User Technical Advisory Board provides feedback to CNCF projects.
cards.explanation: The End User Technical Advisory Board gives CNCF projects feedback on usability, reliability, and performance from an end user perspective.
tags: CNCF End User Technical Advisory Board

cards.statement: CNCF treats production adoption as sufficient evidence for project graduation.
cards.explanation: A CNCF graduation application undergoes broader due diligence, including review of governance and other criteria. Production adoption alone is insufficient.
cards.misconception: Production users alone qualify a CNCF project for graduation.

cards.statement: Kubernetes SIGs focus on defined areas of the project, such as networking or scheduling.
cards.explanation: Special Interest Groups organize ongoing Kubernetes work by technical area, giving contributors a focused place to collaborate.

cards.statement: A KEP records a release announcement after a Kubernetes feature ships.
cards.explanation: A Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal communicates and coordinates a proposed change before the work is completed.
cards.misconception: A KEP is written as a post-release announcement.

cards.statement: The Kubernetes Release Team coordinates release work within SIG Release.
cards.explanation: The Release Team sits within SIG Release and handles the day-to-day work needed to produce Kubernetes releases.

cards.statement: Kubernetes community conduct reports go through the project's public issue tracker.
cards.explanation: Kubernetes directs community conduct reports to its Code of Conduct Committee through a dedicated reporting channel, rather than public issues.
cards.misconception: A public project issue is the reporting channel for conduct incidents.
